headline: Samsung's Indian chip research centre and the Indian Institute of Science have opened a quantum research lab on the institute's Bengaluru campus.
score_reason: Industry-funded teaching and research lab in India; modest scale, no hard performance numbers.
importance_line: It adds shared lab capacity and training for India's quantum and chip workforce, but no experiments or results are announced yet.
summary: The Hindu reports that Samsung Semiconductor India Research and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) inaugurated the lab on 15 Oct 2026, funded through Samsung's corporate social responsibility money, for work on qubit testing, cryogenic electronics, single-photon devices and quantum-device reliability. IISc says it will also open the facility to researchers and students from other institutions in India, as part of a wider effort to build a national quantum talent pool.
notes: Digitimes text cut off (paywall); read The Hindu on the same inauguration.
